newsitem.title: USA: Key GM supplier faces Friday strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: Key GM supplier faces Friday strike deadline.

text.p: General Motors Corp., already battling a strike at an Indiana truck plant, could be forced to shut down virtually all of its North American operations if a key supplier fails to avert a strike threatened Friday.
Delco Remy America Inc., a company made up of former GM parts operations, said Thursday that the United Auto Workers union has set a strike deadline of 11:59 p.m. EST Friday.

The Anderson, Ind.-based company produces starter motors for nearly all of GM's North American-built cars and trucks. It is the second recent GM divestiture to run into difficulty in negotiating a new, separate contract with the UAW this year.
Delco Remy spokesman John Pyzik said negotiations with the UAW were continuing Thursday, but he declined to discuss specific issues or say whether progress was being made.
The company, acquired from GM in 1994 by a managment group headed by former Chrysler Corp. executive Harold Sperlich, employs about 1,600 UAW members at plants in Anderson, Ind., and Meridian, Miss.

Another GM supplier, American Axle & Manufacturing Inc., last month averted a strike when it reached an agreement on a new contract that contained most of the same provisions of the UAW's pattern agreement with GM.
UAW officials were not immediately available to comment on the negotiations. The union has demanded that the new buyers of divested GM operations meet the same terms as the GM agreement.

That includes lump-sum payments of $2,000 in the first year and 3 percent raises in the second and third years, as well as a guarantee to maintain employment at 95 percent of the current work force level over the life of the agreement and generous improvments in pension benefits.

GM is continuing to negotiate with the UAW to end a strike at the automaker's Fort Wayne, Ind., full-size pickup truck plant that started March 14. The major unresolved issue in the dispute are staffing levels required for a new generation of GM pickup trucks due to enter production next year at the plant.
